question: What problems, data representations, architectures, pretraining strategies, and inference methods defined deep-learning research on mathematical reasoning through 2022, and which gaps remained?

key_findings.claim: The survey organizes neural mathematical reasoning by task family, including math word problems, theorem proving, geometry, question answering, and numerically intensive finance, science, and programming applications.
key_findings.evidence: Its taxonomy links each family to representative datasets and output forms rather than treating mathematical reasoning as one benchmark; later tables separate pretrained models, fine-tuning, and in-context methods.

key_findings.claim: Earlier systems commonly encode text with sequence, graph, tree, or attention models and decode an equation, program, proof, graph, or natural-language rationale.
key_findings.evidence: The method review follows the progression from recurrent encoder-decoder systems and syntax-aware graphs to pretrained transformers, and distinguishes answer-only generation from explicit intermediate representations.

key_findings.claim: Pretrained language models shift the field toward self-supervised mathematical corpora, supervised fine-tuning, and example-conditioned inference, but scale does not eliminate basic numeracy defects.
key_findings.evidence: The review catalogs math-specialized pretraining and GPT-style in-context approaches, then notes inconsistent subword segmentations for equivalent number formats and poor extrapolation to large or unseen numbers.

key_findings.claim: In-context reasoning results are highly sensitive to how demonstrations and intermediate steps are selected.
key_findings.evidence: Table 4 contrasts few-shot chain of thought, self-consistency, least-to-most decomposition, learned prompt/example selection, retrieval, automatic chain-of-thought, complexity-based selection, and program-of-thought prompting across math benchmarks.

key_findings.claim: High benchmark accuracy coexists with weak robustness and generalization.
key_findings.evidence: The survey reports sharp degradation under wording or numerical perturbations and highlights out-of-distribution primitives, compositions, and theorem domains as unresolved; it cites SVAMP results well below near-saturated scores on older datasets.

key_findings.claim: Trusted mathematical reasoning requires validation beyond final-answer matching.
key_findings.evidence: Proposed directions include uncertainty and mistake detection, human feedback, theorem-prover feedback, and program execution so that intermediate reasoning can be checked rather than merely read as plausible text.

key_findings.claim: This is a broad narrative map, not a systematic review or a reliable snapshot of the post-2022 LLM reasoning landscape.
key_findings.evidence: The limitations acknowledge selective coverage of the preceding decade and a rapidly changing field; no reproducible search protocol, inclusion flow, quality assessment, or quantitative meta-analysis is provided.

method.core_idea: Synthesize deep-learning approaches to mathematical reasoning through a task-method-representation taxonomy.
method.mechanism: The authors curate work across major mathematical task families, tabulate datasets and representative systems, then organize methods from task-specific neural encoders through pretrained language models and prompting before deriving cross-cutting research challenges.
assumptions: The selected task families adequately represent machine mathematical reasoning.
Reported benchmark results are comparable enough to support qualitative synthesis despite different splits, supervision, and model scales.
Intermediate equations, programs, graphs, proofs, and rationales are meaningful indicators of reasoning rather than only alternative output formats.
A narrative survey can identify durable field-level gaps without a systematic search protocol.

techniques.role: Maps mathematical problem types to benchmarks, inputs, and expected outputs.
Separates equations, programs, proof objects, graphs, and language rationales.
Connects task-specific sequence and graph models to pretrained and in-context learners.
Extracts recurring failures in numeracy, robustness, trust, and multimodal reasoning.

evaluations.setting: Narrative comparison of systems and datasets for word problems, theorem proving, geometry, math QA, and applied quantitative tasks.
evaluations.metric: Published accuracy, exact match, proof success, and task-specific scores.
evaluations.result: The tables show rapid gains within benchmark families but no single evaluation covering all forms of mathematical reasoning.
evaluations.baseline: Earlier task-specific symbolic and neural systems as reported in the cited papers.

evaluations.setting: Review of pretrained-model and in-context-learning results on GSM8K, MultiArith, SVAMP, and related datasets.
evaluations.metric: Final-answer accuracy under fine-tuning and prompting variants.
evaluations.result: Scaling and explicit step prompting improve accuracy, while example selection, decomposition, sampling, and executable programs materially alter outcomes.
evaluations.baseline: Direct answer prediction and ordinary few-shot prompting in the reviewed literature.

evaluations.metric: Performance after lexical, structural, numerical, or distribution shifts.
evaluations.result: Models remain brittle to modest perturbations and struggle with unseen numeric magnitudes and compositions.
evaluations.baseline: In-distribution benchmark results from the same model families.

limitations: The literature-search and inclusion process is not systematic or reproducible.
Results from heterogeneous datasets, splits, model scales, and supervision regimes are juxtaposed without normalized comparison.
Coverage ends before the explosion of reinforcement-learning-trained reasoning models, long test-time reasoning, verifier scaling, and recent formal-math systems.
The survey often relies on final-answer accuracy, which cannot distinguish faithful reasoning from shortcutting or memorization.
Its broad taxonomy gives limited depth on any one subfield and does not quantitatively assess evidence quality.
failure_modes: A benchmark taxonomy can reify historical datasets instead of the underlying mathematical capabilities.
Natural-language rationales may look coherent while containing invalid or causally irrelevant steps.
Contaminated or memorized benchmark items can masquerade as mathematical generalization.
Tokenization changes can confound claims about architectural numeracy.
A rapidly moving survey can become obsolete before publication, especially in prompting and large-model training.
reusable_insights: Evaluate mathematical systems across problem families and distribution shifts, not only one popular benchmark.
Separate answer correctness, intermediate-step validity, proof checking, and calibration as distinct metrics.
Treat number tokenization and representation as experimental variables rather than implementation details.
Use executable programs or formal provers where possible to validate intermediate mathematical claims.
Document dataset, prompt, model, and sampling differences before comparing reported scores.
open_questions: Which benchmark suite best separates memorization, arithmetic execution, abstraction, and proof-level generalization?
How should faithful reasoning be measured when many valid derivations exist?
Can number representations extrapolate systematically without sacrificing ordinary language modeling?
What combinations of neural generation and formal verification scale to research-level mathematics?
How should post-2022 reinforcement learning and test-time compute results revise this taxonomy?

competitive_landscape.title: Large Language Models for Mathematical Reasoning: Progresses and Challenges
competitive_landscape.relationship: Later survey focused specifically on the LLM-era mathematical landscape.
competitive_landscape.difference: Ahn et al. foreground LLM problem types, datasets, techniques, and concerns after the prompting boom; Lu et al. cover a longer arc from task-specific deep learning and a wider set of formal and applied task families.

competitive_landscape.title: A Survey on Large Language Models for Mathematical Reasoning
competitive_landscape.relationship: Current successor survey covering reinforcement learning and test-time scaling.
competitive_landscape.difference: Wang et al. organize 2025 methods around comprehension, answer generation, supervised fine-tuning, RL, extended chain of thought, and test-time scaling, all largely absent from the 2022 snapshot.

competitive_landscape.title: Solving Quantitative Reasoning Problems with Language Models
competitive_landscape.relationship: Contemporaneous primary demonstration of math-specialized large-language-model pretraining.
competitive_landscape.difference: Minerva contributes large-scale quantitative experiments and data curation; the survey situates this approach among task-specific models, representations, and prompting methods without reproducing it.

competitive_landscape.title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models
competitive_landscape.relationship: Foundational prompting method central to the survey's in-context reasoning section.
competitive_landscape.difference: Wei et al. empirically establish chain-of-thought gains at scale; Lu et al. compare it with selection, decomposition, sampling, and program-based variants and emphasize unresolved robustness.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The survey claims a comprehensive synthesis of deep learning for mathematical reasoning across tasks, datasets, neural methods, pretrained models, and future challenges.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: Its enduring contribution is the broad task-and-representation map and early identification of numeracy, robustness, and validation gaps. It is useful historical context rather than a current state-of-the-art guide, and its unsystematic selection prevents evidence-weighted conclusions.

reviewer_notes: Read the complete 25-page extraction, including task and dataset taxonomy, neural and pretrained methods, Table 4 prompting comparison, numeracy and robustness discussion, future work, limitations, appendices, and references. Current successor surveys and the primary Minerva and chain-of-thought sources were checked on arXiv on 2026-08-23.
